entries.name: Lookup table
entries.definition: A table of precomputed values indexed by an input, used to replace repeated calculation with a quick lookup.

entries.name: Low-code development platform
entries.definition: A software platform for building applications mainly through visual modelling and configuration instead of hand-written code.

entries.name: Low risk neonatal nursing
entries.definition: Nursing care of healthy newborns and those with minor health problems, usually in a normal newborn nursery.

entries.name: Low Voltage Transistor-Transistor Logic
entries.definition: A digital logic signalling standard that uses transistor-transistor logic levels at a lower supply voltage, typically 3.3 volts.

entries.name: Luigi
entries.definition: A Python library from Spotify for building and scheduling pipelines of batch jobs that depend on one another.

entries.name: Lumion
entries.definition: 3D rendering software that architects and designers use to turn building models into images, videos and walkthroughs.

entries.name: Lymphedema management
entries.definition: Assessing and treating lymphedema with techniques such as manual lymph drainage, compression and exercise.

entries.name: M2Crypto
entries.definition: A Python library that wraps OpenSSL to provide encryption, SSL/TLS and certificate handling.

entries.name: Machine learning
entries.definition: Building and evaluating models that learn patterns from data.

entries.name: Machine operation
entries.definition: Setting up, running and monitoring machinery to make goods or carry out a process.

entries.name: Machine tools
entries.definition: Power-driven machines, such as lathes and milling machines, that cut or shape metal and other materials.

entries.name: Machining technology
entries.definition: The processes, machines and tools used to shape workpieces by cutting material away.

entries.name: Macintosh Application Environment
entries.definition: Apple software from the mid-1990s that let Mac OS applications run on Unix workstations.

entries.name: macOS
entries.definition: Apple's operating system for Mac computers, called OS X or Mac OS X before 2016.

entries.name: Mail distribution
entries.definition: Sorting incoming mail and packages and delivering them to the right people or departments in an organisation.

entries.name: Mail processing
entries.definition: Receiving, opening, sorting and routing incoming and outgoing mail.

entries.name: Mainframe storage
entries.definition: The disk and tape storage systems, and the software that manages them, used with mainframe computers.

entries.name: Malware analysis
entries.definition: Examining malicious software to understand how it works, what it does and how to detect or remove it.

entries.name: Mammalian cell culture
entries.definition: Growing cells taken from mammals in a laboratory under controlled conditions so they can be studied or used.

entries.name: Manure spreader
entries.definition: Farm machinery that spreads manure over fields as fertiliser.

entries.name: Map production
entries.definition: Compiling, designing and publishing maps from geographic data.

entries.name: Map reading
entries.definition: Interpreting the symbols, scale and features of a map to find locations and plan routes.

entries.name: MapDB
entries.definition: A Java library that provides maps, sets and other collections backed by an embedded database engine on disk or in memory.

entries.name: Margin lending
entries.definition: Lending money to investors so they can buy securities, with the securities held as collateral.

entries.name: Marine navigation
entries.definition: Finding a vessel's position and plotting and following its course at sea.

entries.name: Marine radar
entries.definition: Radar equipment used on ships to detect other vessels, land and hazards.

entries.name: Marionette.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript library built on Backbone.js that adds application structure, composite views and event handling for single-page apps.

entries.name: Maritime law enforcement
entries.definition: Enforcing laws and regulations at sea and in ports, for example by patrolling, boarding vessels and stopping smuggling or illegal fishing.

entries.name: Market capitalization
entries.definition: The total market value of a company's shares, found by multiplying the share price by the number of shares outstanding.

entries.name: Market depth
entries.definition: A measure of how many buy and sell orders sit at different prices, showing how large a trade a market can absorb without the price moving much.

entries.name: Marketing management
entries.definition: Planning, coordinating and overseeing an organisation's marketing work, from research and strategy to campaigns and results.

entries.name: Marketing strategy
entries.definition: Deciding which customers, offers and channels a business will focus on to meet its marketing goals.

entries.name: Masonry
entries.definition: The craft of building walls and structures by laying bricks, stone or concrete blocks with mortar.

entries.name: Mass media
entries.definition: The study of the channels, such as press, broadcasting and online platforms, that reach large audiences.

entries.name: Massage
entries.definition: Working the muscles and soft tissue of the body by hand to ease tension and pain or to help a person relax.

entries.name: Master production records
entries.definition: Controlled documents that set out the materials, steps and checks for making a product batch in regulated manufacturing.

entries.name: Material flow
entries.definition: How raw materials, parts and finished goods move through a plant or supply chain, and how that movement is planned and tracked.

entries.name: Materials testing
entries.definition: Measuring the strength, hardness and other physical or chemical properties of materials to check they meet a specification.

entries.name: Mathematica
entries.definition: Wolfram's software system for symbolic and numerical computation, visualisation and programming.

entries.name: Mathematics
entries.definition: The study of numbers, quantities, shapes and patterns, and of the logical reasoning used to prove facts about them.
